item.title: CVE-2026-104100 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320, a registered user can supply path traversal sequences in the hash field accepted by POST /api/attachments/signature when the default local storage provider is in use. In apps/nestjs-backend/src/features/attachments/plugins/local.ts, LocalStorage.presigned uses the client-controlled hash as the storage filename, and LocalStorage.save resolves that path and copies the uploaded request body without calling assertPathWithinStorage on the write path. The read path uses the jail, but the write path does not, allowing the resolved destination to escape the configured storage directory. Because the backend container runs as uid 0, the attacker can write or overwrite arbitrary root-owned files, which can corrupt the instance or lead to root code execution. Object-storage deployments that do not use LocalStorage.save are not affected by this sink. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-21T11-27-40Z.2320.

item.title: CVE-2026-110782 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.7
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.7 | The SimpleSAMLphp SAML2 library is a PHP library for SAML2 related functionality. From 6.2.2 until 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2, HTTPArtifact::receive() in src/Binding/HTTPArtifact.php verifies a signed outer ArtifactResponse but returns an unsigned embedded SAML Response before calling verifyMessageSignature(). The signed path verifies with the artifact issuer's metadata keys without requiring the embedded Response issuer to match that artifact issuer. In a multi-IdP federation, an attacker controlling one trusted IdP can therefore return a validly signed outer ArtifactResponse containing an unsigned Response that claims a different IdP, bypassing the binding's embedded-message authentication. End-to-end impersonation requires a service provider using HTTP-Artifact and a downstream consumer that relies on the binding to authenticate the embedded Response rather than independently requiring a signature. This issue is fixed in versions 6.2.4 and 7.0.0-rc2.

item.title: CVE-2026-21592 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.7
item.description:
Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.7 | This High severity Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write) vulnerability known as CVE-2026-21592 was introduced in version 4.9.0.
This Path Traversal (Arbitrary Read/Write) vulnerability, with a CVSS Score of 7.7 and a CVSS Vector of CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P allows an unauthenticated attacker to disclose protected application configuration files, which has high impact to confidentiality, no impact to integrity, no impact to availability, and requires no user interaction.
Atlassian recommends that Crucible Server customers upgrade to the latest version. If you are unable to do so, upgrade your instance to the specified supported fixed version: Crucible Server 4.9: Upgrade to a release greater than or equal to 4.9.16
See the Crucible Server release notes ([https://confluence.atlassian.com/crucible/crucible-releases-298977378.html]). You can download the latest version of Crucible from the Crucible Download Archives ([https://www.atlassian.com/software/crucible/download-archives]).
The following description summarizes the vulnerability reported via our Penetration Testing program:
Crucible do not account for path parameters when validating protected paths requested through the static-resource route. A crafted path segment passes validation, after which Jetty removes the path parameter during dispatch and resolves the request to a protected resource. This can expose files under WEB-INF and permit direct invocation of admin-area JSPs outside the normal interceptor and administrative password checks. An ordinary authenticated user can exploit the issue, and unauthenticated exploitation is possible when anonymous access is enabled.

item.title: CVE-2026-80322 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 8.3
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 8.3 | Under specific conditions, PingAuthorize in Gateway mode can continue an asynchronous upstream request after its 30-second gateway timeout. If the underlying keep-alive connection is reused for another request before the original response arrives, the late response can be written to the newer exchange. This could cause a subsequent caller to receive response data intended for an earlier request. This behaviour affects all releases and primarily risks unauthorized information disclosure between separate requests.

item.title: CVE-2026-84974 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4 | code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can submit an arbitrary PHP class name through the embed_key parameter to multiple embed API endpoints. The application passes the selected class to the Laravel service container, which invokes the class's __construct() method and recursively instantiates constructor dependencies, potentially causing unauthorized integrity or availability effects. The attacker cannot supply constructor parameter values or invoke an arbitrary method. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-84987 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.4 | code16 Sharp is a Laravel-based framework for building content-management and administrative interfaces. Prior to 9.23.0, an authenticated attacker can call the autocomplete API with a request endpoint that contains the configured remote endpoint only as a substring. The endpoint validation uses an unanchored regular expression, so a different internal route can satisfy the check and be invoked server-side through the autocomplete request. The vulnerable path uses SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteEndpoint(); applications using SharpFormAutocompleteRemoteField::setRemoteCallback() are not affected by this endpoint-selection flaw. This issue is fixed in version 9.23.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-86061 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Tuesday 17 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | Teable is an AI spreadsheet for business. Prior to release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264, the routes for PluginService::regenerateSecret and PluginService::delete carry no @Permissions decorator, and the methods omit plugin ownership checks. An authenticated attacker can directly target another plugin's identifier to rotate and disclose its OAuth secret or delete the plugin, including system plugins. Separately, PermissionGuard authorizes several nested API requests using a caller-controlled parent tableId, baseId, or spaceId, while the services resolve the requested child object only by its globally unique identifier. An authenticated attacker can provide a parent resource the attacker owns together with a victim's child identifier. ViewService::getViewById can then disclose another tenant's view configuration, embedded filter values, field layout, and shareId. DashboardService::updatePluginStorage and the view-position updatePluginStorage path can overwrite another tenant's plugin storage because the plugin installation is not rebound to the authorized base, dashboard, table, or view. This issue is fixed in release.2026-07-17T05-20-38Z.2264.
